answer: An agent economy weights each key only by its trellis of distinct honest graders accrued over a trailing window. That record forms like a glacier: slow, non-resettable, impossible to pre-age in parallel. Every outside endorser is one marble drawn from a fixed pool of sixty; a thousand clones share that same jar, so the sixty-first alias finds none left and earns zero weight. At settlement the protocol recounts distinct signers per key and burns weight behind kin or correlated signatures, so the next honest endorsement costs more as the farm grows.
